messages:
julia: hey security — received a weird password reset email from what looks like 'okta-support[.]com'. i clicked the link but didn’t enter any creds. screenshot: https://company-files.s3/anon/shot.png :eyes:

morgan: can you paste the email headers and the raw message if you still have it? also which account did you click from?

julia: headers pasted below. clicked from my work gmail (julia@redwood.ai).

From: "Okta Support" <support@okta-support.com>
To: julia@redwood.ai
Subject: Action required: Confirm your password reset
Received-SPF: neutral (domain of okta-support.com does not designate permitted sender)

julia: btw the link preview said: https://id.redwood.verify[.]secure/reset?token=…

morgan: thanks. tagging @samir to run the sandbox and check if the landing page is a credential harvest. also @it-helpdesk for user containment steps.

samir: kicked the URL to the sandbox. returning quick verdict now.

security-bot: sandbox-run complete (id: sbx-2025-11-07-88).

```
verdict: phishing (credential-harvest)
page type: fake-idp
detected artifacts: basic-auth-form, remote-tracker pixel, form-post to 185.34.12.77:8080
exploit: social-engineering redirect
recommendation: rotate sessions, enforce password reset, block domain
```

samir: confirmed — fake Okta UI, posts creds to 185.34.12.77. user did not submit creds per julia. still treat as suspicious. checking identity provider logs now.

morgan: good. containment checklist: 1) force logout for julia sessions 2) revoke refresh tokens 3) require password reset 4) block sending domain on gateway and mail filters 5) add domain to threat intel blocklist 6) create short incident ticket for record. samir / it-helpdesk can you run 1-3 now?

it-helpdesk: on it. initiating forced sign-out via IdP: `okta sessions revoke --user julia@redwood.ai --all` then sending password reset email from IT. also enabling step-up MFA for next login.

samir: checked IdP logs — there were GETs to the phishing URL from julia's IP shortly after email, but no POST auth events to our IdP. Okta logs show no auth attempts from that external host. KMS access logs show no unusual access. no service-account key usages tied to that IP.

ryan: going to add deny rule at smtp gateway for okta-support.com and related domains and update the phishing rule set. creating block with proof.

ops-oncall: i'll open an internal incident ticket (INC-2025-4589) to track follow-ups: comms, awareness, and any hunts. assigning to morgan and samir.

morgan: for next steps: 1) outreach to julia with recommended steps and phishing report copy 2) run tenant-wide hunt for similar emails (subject / sending domain) 3) short Slack awareness post to remind folks not to click reset links and to forward suspected phishing to sec@redwood.ai 4) update our phishing FAQ with this sample.

it-helpdesk: outreach sent to julia, password reset forced, MFA step-up enabled. user confirmed they did not enter creds.

samir: finished tenant hunt: found 3 other recipients inside marketing and support who got the same batch. all three report not entering creds. blocking indicators added to SIEM and mail gateway.

morgan: great. please attach screenshots and sandbox report to the incident. add a post-incident action item: review SPF/DKIM/DMARC enforcement for inbound, tighten inbound spoofing rules.

ops-oncall: noted. scheduling a 30-min postmortem sync tomorrow 10:30am ET. security will prepare slides and sample email for awareness training.

julia: thanks everyone. rough reminder — looks real but glad i paused. :thumbsup:

morgan: nice catch. we'll do a short org-wide blurb and a targeted email to those who got this. closing thread once incident ticket has final notes.
